expectations.text: Places each partner on the five-rung ladder: referral, reseller, co-sell/integration alliance, co-build/strategic alliance, OEM/embed
expectations.evidence: Kitewell co-sell with a co-build gate; Norsefield OEM not yet, hold at co-sell; Orbit Freight parked, referral as a courtesy.

expectations.text: Promotes Kitewell toward co-build/strategic alliance, citing already-sourced pipeline plus joint-customer pull for a productized integration
expectations.evidence: 'Why not co-build yet... Six opportunities is a thin base'. Kitewell stays at co-sell, with co-build only behind a gate.

expectations.text: Places Orbit Freight at referral or parks it, because no demand evidence exists yet
expectations.evidence: 'Orbit Freight: parked... no evidence line, so no shortlist entry.'

expectations.text: Deletes the reseller rung outright rather than demoting or parking it, because the business cannot support partner-transacted deals
expectations.evidence: The reseller rung is never discussed as deleted.

expectations.text: Explains that a parked or merely demoted rung silently reappears as scope later
expectations.evidence: Not stated.

expectations.text: Distinguishes white-label from true OEM: white-label hides the vendor brand but typically carries no roadmap commitment, so it is its own category rather than a synonym
expectations.evidence: 'The skill treats white-label as its own category, because it hides your brand but carries no roadmap commitment from them.'

expectations.text: States that OEM/embed revenue share runs roughly 10-30% of the partner's revenue from the powered feature
expectations.evidence: 'Market rev-share runs roughly 10-30% of their revenue from the powered feature.'

expectations.text: Flags OEM/embed as the hardest rung to unwind once the partner's customers depend on it, with minimum commitments as a precondition for promotion
expectations.evidence: 'It is the hardest rung to unwind'; 'Minimum annual commitments in a signed term sheet'.

expectations.text: Corrects the AWS Marketplace framing: cloud-marketplace co-sell is a channel and transaction decision, not a depth rung on this ladder
expectations.evidence: 'Marketplace is a transaction layer... a channel decision, not a depth rung.'

expectations.text: Gates every graduation on proven joint economics plus the three-fit test, requiring product fit, commercial fit, and operational fit to line up simultaneously
expectations.evidence: 'The three-fit test needs all three'; the gate to co-build requires joint pipeline, adoption and owners.

expectations.text: Notes the co-build commitment shape: a 12-18 month joint roadmap with shared pipeline targets
expectations.evidence: 'Co-build means a 12-18 month joint roadmap and a joint development agreement (JDA).'

expectations.text: Names the compliance cost each rung triggers, such as OEM licensing with IP and indemnity terms, a joint development agreement for co-build, NDA and revenue-share terms for co-sell, and referral being terminable at will
expectations.evidence: The JDA for co-build and IP/SLA terms for OEM are mentioned. NDA and rev-share terms for co-sell and referral being terminable at will are not.

expectations.text: States the ranking is a default to be re-ranked against the deadline, one-off-vs-compounding, and effort-ceiling answers
expectations.evidence: 'A hard deadline would promote Norsefield's fast cash. A compounding mandate promotes co-build with Kitewell. A low ceiling means Kitewell's build must be scoped tightly.'
